agent_note: Heavily aphoristic quote set: 15 of 26 are gnomic (present-tense generalization about pandemics, time, apocalypse, second-person universals), which is exactly the false-present bias METHODOLOGY warns about. Only 6 event quotes, 4 past / 2 present. The past ones are third-person narration of named characters (Olive, Jessica, an unnamed 'she'); the present ones are a first-person reflective voice ('I've been thinking... lately') and a present-tense character state for Edwin. That pattern suggests multiple strands narrated in different tenses rather than one stance, but 6 event quotes is too thin to call which dominates, so narrating_situation is unclear rather than retrospective. Quotation marks survive on ~5 quotes; several unmarked essayistic passages (q07568, q07578, q07581, q07582) carry speech markers and panel/lectern framing elsewhere in the set, so they may be stripped-mark dialogue -- bucketed gnomic on content, noted individually.
